clue.text: Draw back as fellow left island

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
inch is a Scottish word for a small island, as in Inchcolm

explanation.surface: Someone recoils as a companion quits an island.
explanation.walkthrough: INCH as 'island' comes from Scottish place names such as Inchkeith; the crossword uses it freely.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch is to recoil or pull away suddenly, which is drawing back.

clue.text: Stinking way to hide a handkerchief

indicators.note: hiding a thing puts it out of sight within another, so a goes inside

parts.note: foul means stinking
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A smelly route to conceal a hanky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to hide' puts the A into the join of the two words; 'Stinking way' reads as one phrase in the surface but gives two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Foulard is a light silk fabric, and a square of it worn or carried is a handkerchief or scarf.

clue.text: I study the equipment, holding it up as a likeness

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece is held within the others

parts.note: a den is a private room for study or work
kit is gear or equipment

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word it is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone examines the gear, raising it up as a lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses 'it' in this down clue, and 'holding' places that turned pair between the study and the kit.
explanation.definitionFit: An Identikit picture is a police composite of a suspect's face, built to resemble the person.

clue.text: Browbeat core movement within the Church of England

indicators.note: within puts the rearranged letters inside the abbreviation

parts.note: CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England

indicators.note: movement means the letters of core are moved around

explanation.surface: A core faction within the Anglican church bullies others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'movement' rearranges the letters of 'core', and 'within' sets them inside the Church of England's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce is to force by threats or pressure, as a bully intimidates.

clue.text: European legislator started to handle a relative amount of stress

parts.note: an MP, member of parliament, is a lawmaker

indicators.note: the starts of the two words handle and a are taken, one letter from each

parts.note: sis, short for sister, is a family relative

explanation.surface: A Euro politician begins handling a relative measure of strain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'started to' takes the first letters of 'handle' and 'a', giving HA; 'relative' looks like part of the definition but supplies SIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is the weight or accent placed on a word or idea, a quantity of stress.

clue.text: Nothing in a person's complaint

indicators.note: in shows the zero goes inside the word for a person

parts.note: a man is a person; the 's is a link meaning is
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing in a person is a grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a grumble or grievance voiced aloud.

clue.text: Have a wet spell? On the contrary!

indicators.note: contrary means perverse, contrary to the right order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Expecting a wet spell? The opposite: a hot dry one.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for rain, and the answer is its contrary, a hot dry spell, made from the letters of HAVE A WET.
explanation.definitionFit: A heatwave is a period of very hot weather, a spell in the meteorological sense.

clue.text: Penniless relations found in the street

indicators.note: found in shows the relatives sit inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street
kin are relatives

explanation.surface: Broke relatives turn up living rough on the street.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT is British slang for having no money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being skint means having no money at all, being broke.

clue.text: Add up to hot city element

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for add is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: plus means add
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Things total up to a heated city element.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Add up' reads as one phrase meaning total, but 'up' is the reversal signal working on the word for add in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Sulphur is a yellow chemical element, number 16 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Arrangement of new venue was far from smooth

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things in a new order, so the letters that follow are reordered

explanation.surface: The way a new venue was laid out made it bumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement of' rearranges VENUE to UNEVE; the N of 'new' ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uneven has a rough, irregular surface, the opposite of level and flat.

clue.text: Feverish music sung in the shopping precinct

indicators.note: the word in tells us one piece sits within the other here

parts.note: a mall is a shopping precinct or centre
an aria is a song for solo voice in an opera

explanation.surface: Someone feels feverish hearing piped singing in a shopping centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaria brings recurring fevers, so malarial describes a feverish condition.

clue.text: Showing no reaction to short holiday from Open University in America

parts.note: vac is a short form of vacation, a holiday

indicators.note: in shows the university initials sit inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is the abbreviation for the United States, America

explanation.surface: A brief break from distance learning in the States leaves someone blank.
explanation.walkthrough: The Open University is Britain's distance-learning university; 'in' sets its initials inside America's, after the short holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuous look is empty and expressionless, betraying no thought or response.

clue.text: Dictatorial person thrown out at car works

indicators.note: works here means is worked into a new form, so the letters out at car are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tyrant is ejected from a car factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown' adds to the anagram signal: the letters of OUT AT CAR are thrown about and 'works' them into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An autocrat rules with absolute power, a dictator in all but name.

clue.text: Caught in society with false hair

indicators.note: the word in shows the catch letter goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught out in high society wearing a wig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the cricket letter for caught inside the society letter plus 'with', just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A switch is a hank of detached hair worn to add bulk to a hairstyle, a hairpiece.

clue.text: Charged with energy, young socialite turns up to make mischief

indicators.note: in a down clue turns up means the pieces are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a live wire is charged with electrical energy
a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering society

explanation.surface: An energetic debutante shows up to cause trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reverses LIVE plus DEB, giving BED and EVIL; 'with energy' belongs to 'Charged', not a separate E.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to torment or plague, causing trouble and harm.

clue.text: Nobleman ready to capture knight

indicators.note: capturing takes something in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: due means expected or ready, as in due to leave
K is the abbreviation for knight in British honours, as in KBE and KCB

explanation.surface: An aristocrat is poised to seize a knight, as in chess.
explanation.definitionFit: A duke is the highest rank of the British peerage, a titled aristocrat.

clue.text: Marvellous cover up for the inspector

parts.note: super is an informal word for marvellous
a visor is a shield that covers up the face or eyes

explanation.surface: A great cover-up suits the investigating official.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor oversees and checks others' work, as an inspector does.

clue.text: Pay out about a pound on our magnificent display

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the next piece comes after
about means around, so the spending word goes round the pound sign

parts.note: spend means pay out money
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Spending a pound on ourselves makes a grand show.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEND goes 'about' L to give SPLEND, with OUR set 'on' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Splendour is grandeur or magnificence, a brilliant show.

clue.text: United to fetch the girl

parts.note: get means fetch
her refers to a girl

explanation.surface: Someone goes to collect their sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Together means joined or combined as one, like a united pair.

clue.text: Made known that, without yen, country died out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are in disorder and must be rearranged
without means lacking, so the letter for yen is removed

parts.note: Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: It was revealed that a nation, short of money, perished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops Y from COUNTRY to leave COUNTR; with DIED that gives ten letters, which 'out' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To introduce someone is to present them, making them acquainted with others.

clue.text: I'm badly upset by stimulant

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are put in a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone is greatly disturbed by a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram signal but is the fodder: 'badly' rearranges it after the letters of I'm.
explanation.definitionFit: Impetus is a driving force that spurs action, something that stimulates.

clue.text: Card of association

definitions.meaning: a playing card of the black suit marked with trefoils
a society of people sharing an interest, such as a golf or book group

explanation.definitionFit: Clubs are one of the four suits in a card pack, and a club is also a membership society.

clue.text: Speculator set off some shots

parts.note: a bull is a stock-market speculator betting prices will rise

indicators.note: off means out of order, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A trader triggers a volley of gunfire.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullets are the projectiles fired from guns, each one a shot.

clue.text: Items on the table finish up in the cooker

indicators.note: in places the word for finish inside the stove

parts.note: an Aga is a large British range cooker
end means finish

explanation.surface: The dishes end up in the stove.
explanation.walkthrough: An AGA is a heavy cast-iron range cooker found in many British country kitchens; 'up' only links. 'Table' is the meeting table, not the dinner table.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda lists the matters to be discussed at a meeting, the business tabled.

clue.text: Peg will try to stop the hands working

definitions.meaning: a pointed stake driven into the ground, as in a fence

definitions.text: will try to stop the hands working
definitions.meaning: strikers stationed at a workplace who try to keep other workers, the hands, from going in

explanation.definitionFit: A pointed fence stake shares its name with a group of strikers barring workers' entry.

clue.text: The locum insisted some herbal seeds

indicators.note: some means part of, so the answer is a run of letters within the words

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor demands certain spice seeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Cumin is an aromatic seed used as a spice, from a plant of the parsley family.

clue.text: Inclined towards loading a revolver

indicators.note: a revolver is something that turns round, so the letters of loading a are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is tempted to load a handgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolver' looks like a gun but is the anagram signal; 'towards' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A diagonal line slants across, running at an angle, so it is sloping.

clue.text: Was injured on motorway, so crawled

indicators.note: in a down clue on means the next piece comes after
injured means damaged, so the letters of was are knocked into a new order

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A driver got hurt on the motorway and so had to inch along.
explanation.walkthrough: The crawl here is the swimming stroke, not inching along.
explanation.definitionFit: The crawl is a swimming stroke, so having crawled one swam.

clue.text: Missile for the brave

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and the missile is the axe such a warrior throws

explanation.definitionFit: A tomahawk is the light war axe of North American peoples, often thrown.

clue.text: Arrive home first with the money

indicators.note: first places the word for home before the word for arrive

parts.note: in means at home
come means arrive

explanation.surface: A worker gets home first and collects the cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Income is the money one earns or receives over a period.

clue.text: Symptoms of having made mistakes, it's said, with capital

indicators.note: it's said marks a word that is spoken, so it gives the sound not the spelling

parts.note: sinned means having done wrong
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Errors made in a capital city show their tell-tale signs.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a set of signs that together mark a particular condition.

clue.text: Sign that the first gold rush was cut short

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word the

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter of rush is lopped off

explanation.surface: The original gold rush was halted early.
explanation.definitionFit: Taurus, the bull, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.
